newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Nusamba said buying state banks' shares in Astra.
newsitem.headline: Nusamba said buying state banks' shares in Astra.

text.p: A group to which President Suharto is linked has reached an agreement to buy state-owned bank shares in car manufacturer Astra International, bringing its stake to around 10 percent, the Kompas daily said on Saturday.
The newspaper quoted Nusamba group commissioner Muhamad "Bob" Hasan as saying it had reached an agreement to buy all the shares in Astra owned by state-owned banks and their pension funds.
Astra is Indonesia's largest vehicle manufacturer.

"We have an agreement with government banks and their pension funds to buy shares that they want to sell," Hasan was quoted as saying by Kompas, adding that the transaction will take place sometime next week.
Hasan said that Nusamba had reached an agreement to buy the stock at slightly above market prices.
"If the market price is 3,950 (rupiah), then we have agreed a buy-sell price slightly higher than this," Hasan was quoted as saying. Kompas said the price would be 4,000 rupiah.
Shares in Astra closed on Friday at 4,000 rupiah.

As of October 9, the Indonesian Export-Import Bank (Bank EXIM), its employee foundation and two pension funds owned by Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) had a combined stake of 9.61 percent in Astra, Kompas said.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.
Astra is a widely-held company and brokers have said an 18-20 percent stake may be sufficient to gain a controlling interest.
